key_insight: A fully discrete finite element Chorin projection scheme converges along a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic incompressible Navier–Stokes equations in two and three dimensions.
engineering_relevance: The result provides a mathematical foundation for finite element simulation of incompressible flows with multiplicative stochastic forcing.
method: Split each time step into predicted and divergence-corrected velocity approximations.
Establish solvability and uniform moment bounds, using numerical dissipation to identify a common velocity limit.
Combine spatial–temporal estimates with Aldous’ tightness criterion to prove subsequence convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence analysis in 2D and 3D and numerical experiments in 2D with smooth and vortex sheet initial data, without quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: The theorem requires stable, approximating finite element spaces and a mesh–time-step coupling condition; it does not establish a convergence rate.
paper_title: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
